correctness.rationale: The explicit positive definite matrix P has det P=qz²[1-q/(1+qz)²]>0. Exact evaluation of the two companion matrices yields E[A_D^T P A_D]-P=[z(qz²+z-2)/(1+qz)]diag(1,0). Two-step observability is strictly positive for every q in (0,1) and z>0, proving contraction, conservation, or growth in mean-square energy precisely on the three sides of z+qz²=2. Independence of centered innovations adds exactly sigma² per energy step. Stationary second moment and pole follow algebraically; the separate Jury test establishes the first/second-moment stability gap. value.rationale: Independent zero/one-step gradient staleness is a natural mathematical model of asynchronous numerical optimization. The result gives a sharp closed-form staleness budget rather than merely sufficient bounds, quantifies the stationary noise blow-up, and proves a strict parameter window where expected iterates converge although mean-square energy grows. The positive quadratic energy identity is structural and can serve as a check for general delay-stability estimates; scope beyond the scalar Bernoulli fixed-step model is explicitly unproved.
